- Approval-Prüfung und lokaler Write sind serialisiert/idempotent; stale, manipulierte, parallele oder serverübergreifend alte Refs sollen fail-closed behandelt werden. Provider-Ausführung existiert weiterhin nicht.

Failures and how to do differently:

- Der aktuelle Hardening-Diff wurde noch nicht unabhängig final reviewt, nicht vollständig getestet, nicht committet und nicht gepusht. Das darf nicht als abgeschlossen beschrieben werden.
- Keine echte Gmail-/IMAP-Mailbox wurde in diesem Slice gelesen; keine Credentials erfinden oder protokollieren und keinen Live-Source-Proof vor Abschluss des Hardening-Slices starten.

### Task 2: WebMCP project evaluation

task: determine where WebMCP is useful for live deployments

task_outcome: success

- WebMCP exposes structured callable tools to a browser agent; it does not replace accessible HTML, SEO, metadata, or normal text extraction.
- Bubblophy’s existing server-side MCP/API should remain authoritative for authentication, authorization, data, and writes. WebMCP can be an optional browser convenience layer for UI-specific actions.

- Do not imply ordinary ChatGPT/Gemini/Copilot chats automatically gain page understanding merely because WebMCP is present.

### Task 1: Backend shared workspace contract and implementation

task: implement shared server-side Curriculum WorkRevision Primary with CAS/recovery and current-account authorization
task_group: novari-education-backend
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- when the user requested Phase 2, they said not to rebuild the whole system, to preserve the existing UI/UX, continue using Orchestrate, commit/push regularly with Commit Writer, and ask for clarification on real uncertainty -> future work should reuse existing Sequence/Fence/EditSession/Recovery/Autosave contracts and checkpoint before risky persistence or migration decisions.
- the user wanted every currently authorized PDL and LMS Support user to work on the same Curriculum overview regardless of creator -> treat `createdBy` as provenance only, not normal access control.

Reusable knowledge:
- Phase 2 uses one version-wide shared server Primary. Current `pdl`/`lmsSupport` authorization is checked server-side on every mutating request; account deactivation or role removal invalidates writes from existing sessions.
- Whole-snapshot Sequence-CAS is the conflict model. Stale writes never silently overwrite; they create a typed Recovery under the same shared Primary. No automatic merge/fork.
- Review, submit, publish, import, exports, topic/structure/GitHub-path operations bind exact shared WorkRevision ID/Sequence/Basis/Fence. Submit/Withdraw are available to PDL and LMS Support; Request Changes/Approve/Reopen/Publish remain PDL-only.
- New takeover mutations return 409 `CURRICULUM_WORK_REVISION_TAKEOVER_NOT_REQUIRED`; historical `handed_over` provenance and exact old receipt replays remain compatible.
- Shared-primary readiness is fail-closed: read-only duplicate preflight, exact unique partial index verification/installation, then serving/background-worker startup. No automatic duplicate cleanup.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Read-only preflight found exactly two `UNIQUE_INDEX_COLLISION` cases for `curriculum_work_revision_shared_primary_open_unique`. Do not install the index, deduplicate, rewrite owners, or perform DB/production writes until a separate manual data decision is explicitly approved.
- Backend startup correctly stops at `INDEX_NOT_READY`; Cron/background workers must start only after DB, index, GitHub, job-recovery, heartbeat, and HTTP-bind readiness. Shutdown must stop timers first.

References:
- branch `refactor/curriculum-workrevision-continuity-phase-2`
- final backend HEAD/remote `257193a233f753d23edef28ee432143319509baa`
- bootstrap safety commit `257193a2`
- exact blocker: `UNIQUE_INDEX_COLLISION` x2 for `curriculum_work_revision_shared_primary_open_unique`

### Task 1: Durable coalesced fallback and failure-path repair

task: Persist newer coalesced Phase-2 snapshots durably and preserve truthful UI state across receipts, unmount, and storage failure.
task_group: Portal WorkRevision autosave/collaboration
 task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user required strict `$orchestrate`/`$scoped-fix`, RED→GREEN TDD, minimal same-slice edits, no browser/server mutation, and no commit/push until final review -> use this gated workflow for similar Phase-3 fixes.
- The user required B to be durable before cleanup, A→B→A coalescing to remain intact, no overlapping writes, and fail-closed behavior on persistence failure -> verify durable IndexedDB state directly, not only refs or UI state.

Reusable knowledge:
- In `src/components/lms/teaching-plan/editor/hooks/useCurriculumWorkAutosave.ts`, a newer fallback snapshot must be persisted immediately through `runCollaborationStoreOperation`/`persistLocal`; `phase2FallbackFollowUpRequestRef` is coordination metadata, not the only storage location.
- Follow-up execution rereads `storeRef.current.getDraft(recordKey)` and sends only the durable snapshot/hash if generation, mount, and hash fences still match.
- Collaboration cleanup must await both `collaborationEventChainRef.current` and `collaborationStoreChainRef.current` before closing IndexedDB; otherwise a blocked B persist can be lost on unmount.
- After an older A server receipt, `SERVER_CONFIRMED` must be followed by `LOCAL_SAVED` when `dirty && !baseIsStale`, yielding truthful `local_only`. Do not apply this over a real `base_stale` receipt.
- If B persistence returns false, the follow-up path must dispatch `LOCAL_FAILED` while mounted; a later A receipt must not overwrite `storage_error` with `server_confirmed` or `base_stale`.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Initial bug: B remained only in a React ref while A was in flight; IndexedDB still contained A after unmount. Fix by serializing immediate durable persistence.
- Cleanup bug: waiting only on the event chain allowed the store to close before B’s blocked persistence completed. Fix by awaiting both event and store chains.
- Status bug: A receipt masked a failed B persistence as `server_confirmed`. Re-dispatch `LOCAL_FAILED` on `followUpPersisted === false`.

References:
- Production locations: `useCurriculumWorkAutosave.ts` around 763–764, 1938–2008, and 4033–4037.
- Regression tests: `src/components/lms/teaching-plan/__tests__/useCurriculumWorkAutosave.collaboration.test.tsx`, including tests named `persists a coalesced opaque follow-up before unmount can discard it` and `keeps a failed coalesced opaque persist visible after the active write confirms`.
- Validation: autosave suite `97/97`; combined Phase-3 matrix `178/178`; focused race tests included unmount, failure, A→B→A, and no-overlap cases.

 task_outcome: success

Reusable knowledge:

task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- Der Nutzer verlangte ausschließlich das JavaScript-Backend und einen eng begrenzten B4b-Scope; die separate TypeScript-Variante darf nicht verwendet werden.
- Der Nutzer verlangte Reuse-first an vorhandenen Controller-/Transaktionsgrenzen, zentrale B4a-Policy/Logger/AuditStore-Kette, keine parallele Auditstruktur, keinen Dualvertrag und keine reale Collection-Löschung.
- Der Nutzer verlangte RED→GREEN-Tests, Privacy-Sentinels, unabhängige Reviews, fokussierte Re-Reviews sowie normalen Commit/Push ohne fremde Änderungen; diese Checkliste ist bei ähnlichen Slice-Aufgaben standardmäßig anzuwenden.

Reusable knowledge:
- Voll- und Teil-Löschung verwenden nun jeweils genau ein zentrales Event: `audit.employee_archive_deleted` bzw. `audit.employee_archive_partial_deleted`, mit `action: delete`, `outcome: success`, `targetType: employee_archive`.
- Fachmutation, Auditpersistenz und Erfolgsausgabe laufen in der bestehenden MongoDB-Transaktionsgrenze. Auditfehler verhindern Erfolg und rollen die fachliche Änderung zurück.
- Der Post-Commit-Audit-Callback wird ausschließlich aus dem finalen Rückgabewert von `withTransaction` ausgeführt. Das verhindert falsche Erfolgsaudits, wenn ein transienter Retry danach mit `400`/`404` endet.
- Tests müssen Query, `save`/Delete und Audit explizit an dieselbe Session binden; ein Fake-Rollback, das unabhängig von der Session zurücksetzt, ist unzureichend.
- Generisches Write-Audit wird für `DELETE /archive/:id/deadline/:category` über `skipGenericWriteAudit` unterdrückt, um Exactly-once zu erhalten.
- `ArchiveAuditLog`-Schema, Import und Schreibpfade wurden entfernt. Es bleiben kein Legacy-Reader, Dual Read/Write, Backfill, Altimport oder Startup-Cleanup.
- Persistierte Auditdaten verwenden zentrale Allowlist-/Hashlogik; Tests bestätigen Abwesenheit von ObjectIds, Mitarbeitername, Freitext, Body/Query, Tokens, Pfaden und Rohfehlern.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Erste unabhängige Reviews fanden: (1) Retry konnte ein altes Erfolgsaudit ausgeben, (2) Rollbacktests erzwangen keine Sessionbindung, (3) Inventar verwies noch pauschal auf B7. ### Task 1: B5 Request-Fehler genau einmal persistieren

task: Implementiere ausschließlich Slice B5 im JavaScript-Backend.
task_group: Novari Logging / Backend Observability
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- Der Nutzer verlangte „ausschließlich Slice B5“, ausschließlich JavaScript-Backend, aktiven Branch `refactor/logging-system`, keinen Worktree/Ersatzbranch und keine B6/B7/B8-Ausweitung -> bei ähnlichen Tasks Scope und Repository strikt begrenzen.
- Der Nutzer verlangte Start-Gate, Reuse-first, begrenzte read-only Scouts, unabhängigen finalen Review, fokussierte plus vollständige Tests, engen Commit und normalen Push -> diese Verifikationsreihenfolge künftig pro Slice beibehalten.
- Der Nutzer verlangte unveränderte sichere Response/`headersSent`/`next(err)`, nicht-blockierende Best-effort-Telemetrie und Privacy ohne Rohfehlerdaten -> diese Punkte sind harte Acceptance Criteria.

Reusable knowledge:
- Der bestehende schema-v1-Store ist `libs/observability/auditStore.js::persistSecurityAuditEvent`; B5 verwendet ihn direkt und nicht `logAuditEvent`, weil letzteres Legacy-Audit-Vokabular und zusätzliche Success-Logs erzeugt.
- `libs/observability/requestErrorEvent.js` koordiniert globalen Handler und direkten Finish/Close-Pfad über einen response-lokalen Claim. Dadurch entstehen pro Request höchstens ein `request.error`-Log und ein relevantes Event.
- `middleware/auditWritePolicy.js` ist eine kleine pure Policy für POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE und teilt Methoden-, Status-, Auth-, Export-/Download-/Preview-/PDF-/Sensitive- und `skipWriteAudit`-Ausschlüsse mit `auditWriteActions.js`; das verhindert Klassifikationsdrift.
- Persistierte B5-Events verwenden ausschließlich feste Codes `REQUEST_WRITE_FAILED` und `REQUEST_UNEXPECTED_ERROR`, `category=error`, `severity=error`, `outcome=failed`, erlaubte Action sowie feste `failedStage`-Werte.
- Persistenz läuft fire-and-forget. Sync-Policyfehler und async Store-Rejections werden enthalten; maximal ein sicherer `request_error.persistence_failed`-Log, kein Retry/Loop/Unhandled Rejection und keine Änderung der ursprünglichen Response.
- Request-ID ist nur Korrelation. Gleiche validierte inbound Request-ID über getrennte Requests darf keine Deduplizierung auslösen; Event-IDs bleiben getrennt.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Der erste unabhängige Review fand einen P1-Fehler: synchron scheiternde Direct-4xx-Klassifikation konnte still ohne Claim und ohne Fehlertelemetrie enden. Fix: Kandidaten bei 400/409/422 oder 5xx fallback-sicher claimen, einmalig `request.error` loggen, bei unklarer Ausschlusslage nicht persistieren und Response unverändert lassen.
- `git fetch origin refactor/logging-system` scheiterte zunächst mit `cannot open '.git/FETCH_HEAD': Operation not permitted`; nach expliziter Berechtigung war der Fetch erfolgreich. Bei eingeschränkter Git-Umgebung Remote-Operationen mit benötigter Berechtigung ausführen.

Preference signals:
- The user required “ausschließlich additive, UNVERDRAHTETE Operation-/Resolver-/Repository-/Code-Primitiven” -> future work must inspect active route and generator imports to prove non-wiring.
- The user prohibited active producer, Student status, final audit, response, outbox, receipt, and lease changes -> keep d1a technical-only and defer cutover to d1b.
- The user required exact server-side environment handling and fail-closed `test`/`staging`/empty/unknown behavior -> never derive environment or paths from client input and never silently fall back to production.

Reusable knowledge:
- Added `CertificateGenerationOperationModel` in `models/certificateGenerationOperationSchema.js`; states are `pending`, `uploading`, `uploaded`, `error`, `finalized`, with fixed technical error codes and unique index `certificate_operation_key_unique` on `operationKey`.
- `certificateOperationRepository.js` atomically claims Student/Course operation and allocates the certificate number using existing `allocateCertNumber(..., { session })`; retries/concurrent duplicate claims reuse the winner.

- `certificateOperationRecovery.js` uses existing HiDrive download/upload primitives to verify matching bytes or overwrite the same deterministic path. Monotonic fencing rejects stale `markUploaded`/`markError` writes.
- Active files `_classManager/controller/certificateCompletionController.js`, `_classManager/controller/certificateGenerationController.js`, `_classManager/controller/certificateController.js`, and `_classManager/routes/courseRouter.js` were checked for absence of operation wiring.

### Task 1: Certificate correction operation foundation

task: Add additive, producer-local, unconnected certificate-correction operation primitives.
task_group: backend certificate correction
 task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user required this slice to remain strictly additive and unconnected: no route/controller/bootstrap wiring, no Student/archive/live-reference/status/audit/response changes, and no real HiDrive upload/delete -> future slices should stop instead of expanding scope.
- The user required explicit visibility for Replica-Set skips and no claims that skipped tests ran -> always report executed tests and skips separately.
- The user required reuse-first investigation, independent review, focused commit, normal push, and final clean `0/0` handoff -> preserve this verification sequence.

Reusable knowledge:
- Operation key is server-derived from Student, course, concrete predecessor document identity, and canonical correction-input SHA-256. Identical canonical input replays the same operation; changed input is blocked while an operation is active; finalized replay is accepted only when result document, content hash, environment, and current live path still match. A→B→A after an intervening document creates a new serial operation.
- Schema states are exactly `pending`, `uploading`, `uploaded`, `references_committed`, `error`, `finalized`; technical failures use fixed codes only.
- Exact index contract: unique `{ operationKey: 1 }`; partial unique `{ studentId: 1, courseId: 1 }` with status `$in: ['pending','uploading','uploaded','references_committed','error']`. Producer-local create/re-read readiness rejects wrong key, uniqueness, partial filter, sparse/hidden/TTL/collation drift, duplicate descriptors, and non-proven readiness.
- Environment resolver accepts only exact `development` and `production`. Development target is `/students/Development Exporte/{studentId}/certificates`; production retains `/students/{studentId}/certificates`. Other values fail before external I/O.
- Upload/recovery binds content SHA-256, deterministic target, environment, and fencing token. It verifies same-target bytes or performs identical overwrite; stale/fence losers do not write status or remote artifacts.
- Cleanup primitive is narrowly bound to the persisted predecessor path and `references_committed`. Exact remote 404 is treated as already deleted; all other failures remain retryable under fixed `CERTIFICATE_CORRECTION_DELETE_FAILED` without provider-body/path leakage.
- D2a deliberately does not call application bootstrap or alter the active correction route. B7a.1d2b must wire readiness before `listen()`, perform the transaction and required audit, then finalize cleanup before HTTP 200.

Failures and how to do differently:
- A sandbox denied initial `git fetch` and `git add`; use approved elevated permission for Git operations when required, then re-check branch, remote, and status.
- Mongoose auto-created the temporary test database before the freshness check. For isolated database tests, connect with `autoCreate: false` and `autoIndex: false`, verify absence, then explicitly create collection/indexes.
- Reviews identified missing environment/path revalidation, incomplete A→B→A coverage, and absent same-target-overwrite/repository-transition tests. Add these checks before final review.
- Real Replica-Set tests require `CURRICULUM_TEST_REPLICA_SET_URI`; without it, the two correction race tests visibly skip. With an approved isolated connection, both real tests passed.

References:
- Commit `2a00cd374cf0faf92450cdb4592f494a15e9baa3`; pushed normally to `origin/refactor/logging-system`.

- Real isolated Replica-Set result: 2 passed, 0 skipped; task-local temporary databases were verified empty and final cleanup reported 0 remaining.
- Regression result: 134 passed, 0 failed, 9 skips. Full suite: 6,945 tests, 6,872 passed, 0 failed, 73 skips. `npm run lint` passed.

### Task 1: F1a central Portal support information

task: Implement strict safe support-copy projection and wire only the three authorized central Portal error producers; commit and push.
task_group: Novari Portal logging/error handling
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user required the “kleinsten zentralen Portal-Teilslice”, an exact 13-file allowlist, no caller migration, no Backend/LMS/F2 scope, and no opportunistic refactoring -> future work must preserve these boundaries and stop on any scope expansion.
- The user repeatedly required “keine weiteren Edits, Formatierungen oder Tests” once a candidate was frozen -> after final verification, do not modify the candidate.
- The user required exact contract/diff/test reporting and independent-review handoff -> report concrete paths, commands, counts, commit hashes, and baseline comparisons rather than generic status.

Reusable knowledge:
- Baseline/start gate for this rollout: repo `/Users/mrbubbles/dev/novari/novari-education-portal`, branch `chore/logging-improvements`, baseline `ed327fed999ffffcdd941f8bcb752ef74ed5a989`, upstream initially 0/0, backend F0 commit available locally.
- F1a uses a separate `extractBackendSupportInformation` in `src/libs/utils/backendError.ts`; legacy `extractBackendErrorDetails` and `src/libs/utils/__tests__/backendError.test.ts` remain unchanged.
- Only a genuine `AxiosError` instance with an own data property `isAxiosError === true` is accepted. The extractor reads own data properties only and wraps the new reflection boundary fail-closed. Inherited getters/accessors and throwing Proxy traps are not executed.
- Valid support projection requires response status 400–599, object-shaped nested `response.data.error`, bounded one-line message, code `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`, valid request ID `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`, and at least one valid request-ID source. If body and header IDs both exist they must match exactly.
- Header arrays, multiple/case-colliding headers, comma-separated values, invalid values, and array header containers are rejected before header enumeration. Regression test at `backendError.supportInformation.test.ts:337-363` proves an array with its own `x-request-id` stays `undefined` and its `ownKeys` trap is not called.
- Timestamp is optional and only derived from exactly one strictly canonical IMF-fixdate `Date` response header, emitted as ISO-UTC. Invalid/missing/multiple/array/falsely zoned dates omit the entire timestamp line; browser time is never used.
- Serializer output is fixed ordered lines with no trailing newline: `Support-Information`, `Meldung`, `Fehlercode`, `Referenz-ID`, `Anwendung: Portal`, static `Bereich`, optional `Zeitpunkt`.
- `actionHint` is excluded entirely; raw details/issues/headers/URLs/queries/IDs/JSON are never copied or projected.
- Authorized central producers are `src/libs/apiClient.ts` (global 500/502/503 interceptor), `src/libs/utils/errorHandling.ts` (handled API path), and the non-warning backend path in `src/libs/utils/error-handler.ts`. Warning, silent, auth retry, skip-global-toast, force behavior, status classification, and direct callers remain compatible.
- `toast.ts` keeps `duration: Infinity`; the safe projection changes the action label to `Support-Information kopieren`, while incomplete envelopes retain legacy `Referenz kopieren` behavior.

Failures and how to do differently:
- A first full-suite run had one timing failure in unchanged `useCurriculumWorkAutosave.collaboration.test.tsx`; the isolated test passed and the repeated full suite passed. Treat isolated transient failures as baseline/flake evidence unless reproducible in touched files.
- Full `npm run lint` had pre-existing failures/warnings only in untouched files; allowlist ESLint passed. Do not “fix” unrelated lint errors outside scope.

Preference signals:
- The user required a “vollständig frischer” repository-bound READ-ONLY review, “findings-first”, exact allowlist, unchanged contracts, and explicit freeze/review/commit boundaries -> future agents should verify scope and ownership before proposing implementation and should not edit or test in review-only mode.
- The user explicitly required preservation of original error identity, Retry, CAS, Continuation, invalidations, Success, Draft/Storage, and Caller behavior -> similar plans should include these as explicit unchanged invariants.

Reusable knowledge:
- Baseline was verified at `0555d5e6781cf1d2f0f8db03cd21b683174fafd0`; branch `chore/logging-improvements` matched origin, upstream `0/0`, worktree clean.
- Eight self-learning service mutations exist, but runtime service calls are routed through `useLmsSelfLearning.ts`; no direct production callers were found outside the hook layer.
- The eight-write hypothesis is invalid as a single-owner slice: `Update Status` and `Attach` are called by the excluded 967-line editor continuation and its shared catch calls `showHandledApiErrorToast` again after hook-level handling. Suppressing the interceptor with `skipGlobalErrorToast` does not suppress this second local toast.
- Corrected slice contains six writes only: Create, Update, Delete, Review-Note, Detach, Reorder. Status and Attach must be a separate follow-up that resolves continuation ownership; the editor remains excluded.
- `src/libs/apiClient.ts` has request-local `skipGlobalErrorToast`, which only suppresses automatic 500/502/503 interceptor toasts. It should be applied per request to the six selected writes, including DELETE config and DELETE-with-data config for detach; do not add it to GETs, Status, or Attach in this slice.
- Existing `showHandledApiErrorToast(title, error)` in `src/libs/utils/errorHandling.ts` is the correct central display path. A backward-compatible optional third argument is appropriate: `showHandledApiErrorToast(title, error, area = title)`. This preserves all existing callers while allowing Update/Delete/Review-Note to retain title `Fehler` but use a static support area such as `Self-Learning-Verwaltung`.
- Do not use `handleError` here: it can alter title, fallback, or console behavior. Do not duplicate strict support projection in hooks.
- Strict support projection is fail-closed: genuine Axios error, status 400–599, complete nested `data.error`, safe message/code/request ID, and validated headers. Invalid envelope with a safe ID uses the existing three-argument reference toast; missing ID/non-Axios uses the existing fallback.
- Focused support tests should cover all six mutations, exact request config/signatures, valid four-argument support toast, invalid three-argument reference toast, missing-ID/non-Axios fallback, hostile fields excluded, original error identity, and exactly one service call. Keep GETs, Status, Attach, continuation, CAS, retry, invalidations, success, drafts/storage, and editor behavior unchanged.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not claim “all eight writes have hook-only ownership” while the editor continuation catch remains unchanged; split Status/Attach into a later owner-resolution slice.
- Do not change titles merely to obtain a static support area; use the optional `area` argument with default `title`.
- Do not broaden into the 967-line editor, reconciliation GETs, adjacent callers, or broad existing tests without a new explicit scope decision.

### Task 1: Recruiting and Lead Process slice boundary

 task_group: Portal Logging V2 F1 planning/review
 task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- When the user requested a “vollständig frischer repositorygebundener READ-ONLY-Plan-Reviewer” with no delegation, edits, tests, formatting, fetch, commit, push, browser, or security scan, future work should use only current repository evidence, fail closed on drift, and report unperformed checks honestly.
- When the user required findings-first output, exact production allowlists, explicit exclusions, and separate Go, future reviews should lead with prioritized findings and never treat plan alignment as implementation authorization.
- The user clarified that size/scope gates concern Production Code; mechanically necessary test files are not the same stop condition. Preserve this distinction.

Reusable knowledge:
- Verified baseline was Portal branch `chore/logging-improvements` at `bf78c29e9854d9f7b29dc734d66a9bfe90ed2a71`; local `origin/chore/logging-improvements` matched, upstream was `0/0`, and worktree/index were clean. Fetch was prohibited, so origin evidence was local only.
- Recruiting and Lead Process share the F1 objective but not a coherent technical slice: separate services, hooks, query keys, components, payloads, success paths, and invalidation owners. Recruiting also has a direct local employee-conversion owner; Lead Process has ten MutationCache-owned mutations.
- Active TanStack writes can receive both Axios-interceptor and Production `MutationCache` error toasts on `500/502/503`. The existing request-local `skipGlobalErrorToast: true` mechanism is the intended minimal deduplication change.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not combine Recruiting and Lead Process merely because both target support information. Their distinct ownership and contract boundaries require two concrete plans.
- Do not change shared `apiClient.ts`, `queryClient.ts`, or the central projector to solve producer-specific ownership.

References:
- `src/libs/apiClient.ts` and `src/libs/queryClient.ts`: global interceptor plus MutationCache ownership.
- `src/libs/applicantService.ts` and `src/libs/leadProcessService.ts`: separate producer surfaces.
- Spec constraint: one repository, exact allowlist, no more than ten Production files without new approval, and every runtime diff mapped to Spec §2.2.

- Baseline war exakt `chore/logging-improvements` bei `e97ee4a44a90be806e28bd65b32dbf9a25cd182b`, sauberem Worktree und Upstream `0/0`.
- Der Risk-POST zur PDF-Erzeugung ist bereits ein kohärenter separater Slice: `src/libs/riskService.ts` sendet bodylos mit `{ skipGlobalErrorToast: true }`; `useGenerateDossierPdf` nutzt einen lokalen Toast-Owner, `retry: 0` und zwei Cache-Invalidierungen. Dieser POST-Slice wurde nicht erweitert.
- Der Preview-GET läuft über `RiskList.tsx` -> `DocumentPreviewModal.tsx`; das Modal ruft `apiClient.get(documentUrl, { responseType: 'blob', signal })` auf, erstellt bei Erfolg eine Objekt-URL und zeigt PDFs per `<object>` inline. Objekt-URLs werden ersetzt, beim Schließen und beim Unmount revokiert.
- Der Axios-Interceptor replayed 401 einmal nach `refreshAuthSession()` mit demselben Request-Config; request-local `skipGlobalErrorToast` bleibt beim Replay erhalten. Ohne Opt-out toastet der Interceptor 500/502/503 global.
- Tatsächliches sichtbares GET-Verhalten: 400/403/409/422 = Inline „Vorschau nicht verfügbar“ mit technischem Axios-Fehlertext, kein Toast; 401 = einmal Refresh/Replay, danach Inline-Fehler; 500/502/503 = globaler persistenter Serverfehler-Toast plus Inline-Fehler; Netzwerk = Inline `Network Error`; Abort wird still ignoriert.
- Axios liefert bei `responseType: 'blob'` JSON-Fehlerkörper als Blob. `extractBackendSupportInformation` verlangt `response.data.error` als Objekt und ruft weder `Blob.text()` noch `arrayBuffer()` auf; der Blob-Fehler kann daher nicht vollständig projiziert werden. `X-Request-Id` aus Headern kann separat als Referenz-ID erhalten bleiben.
- `skipGlobalErrorToast` ist technisch request-local sicher, löst den Preview-Gesamtvertrag aber nicht: Opt-out allein entfernt die Referenz-/Supportkopie, lokaler Toast erzeugt weiterhin Toast-plus-Inline-Doppelowner, und gemeinsames Modal betrifft 16 Konsumenten.
- Der Retry-Button des gemeinsamen Modals ist im Risk-Register faktisch defekt: Schließen setzt `previewRiskId` auf `null` und unmountet das Modal; der spätere `onOpenChange(true)`-Timeout öffnet keine neue Vorschau.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Kein kleiner F1-GET-Slice freigeben, solange Blob-Fehlerdekodierung, Content-Type-/Größen-/Shape-Grenzen, alleiniger Fehlerowner sowie Referenz-ID-/Supportkopie-Vertrag nicht separat entschieden sind.
- Nicht nur den globalen Toast unterdrücken; dadurch würde die bestehende Supportfähigkeit verschlechtert.
- Nicht `DocumentPreviewModal` pauschal für alle 16 Flächen ändern, wenn nur der Risk-Pfad bewertet wird.
- Abort nicht als Nutzerfehler behandeln; das bestehende stille Verhalten ist korrekt.
- Die aktuelle No-Change-Allowlist lautet: 0 Produktionsdateien, 0 Testdateien, 0 Docs/Changelog.

task_group: novari portal onboarding / Logging V2 F1

Preference signals:
- The user required an exact four-file allowlist, hard stop gates, unchanged product/API/workflow behavior, no broad formatting, and findings-first independent review -> keep similar fixes narrowly scoped and stop rather than widening the slice.
- The user required a synchronous QueryClient-bound claim keyed by `userID + response.role + contractStartDate`, robust to StrictMode, remounts, multiple instances, and final failures -> guard automatic mutations synchronously before `mutate`, not with component-local state.
- The user explicitly required real `apiClient` interceptors, production QueryClient, and safe support projection in tests, mocking only deep transport/toast sinks -> preserve real integration boundaries in similar error-owner tests.

Reusable knowledge:
- `OnboardingWidget.tsx` now claims one logical automatic PDF attempt per stable key derived from `userID`, response role, and `contractStartDate`. Only completed and `!pdfGenerated` data qualifies. Final errors retain the claim; StrictMode, concurrent widgets, refetches, rerenders, and remounts do not repost. Confirmed incomplete or already-generated state can release the claim; loading transitions do not.
- `useGenerateOnboardingPdf` posts exactly `apiClient.post('/employees/my-onboarding/generate-pdf', undefined, { skipGlobalErrorToast: true })`, uses local `onError`, `retry: 0`, keeps error identity, invalidates only `['my-onboarding']` on success, and emits no success toast.
- Local error handling first uses `extractBackendSupportInformation`. If that strict envelope is incomplete but `extractBackendErrorDetails` yields a separately valid request ID, it calls persistent `showBackendErrorToast` with a static German fallback and the ID. Without an ID it uses the static fallback `showErrorToast`. Raw message/response/URL/query/payload/PII never enter the toast.
- Final tests: new suites 26/26; relevant block 302/302; full suite 470 files / 5,558 tests; typecheck and focused ESLint green; build green (6,672 modules, known chunk-size warning only); `git diff --check` green. Global lint still has 4 pre-existing errors and 6 warnings outside the allowlist.

- A first reset test was tautological because it began without an existing claim. Establish a real claim before testing confirmed incomplete/pdf-generated reset and requalification.
- A first Widget success test mocked `invalidateQueries` inside the mocked hook, so it could pass if production invalidation was removed. Test direct success through the real hook instead.
- A real Widget integration test initially depended on wall-clock time and would stop qualifying after the two-day completion window. Use fake timers and fixed system time for date-dependent onboarding tests; restore real timers in `afterEach`.

### Task 1: Employee Feedback PDF F1 producer analysis

task_group: novari-portal-logging-v2-f1
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- when planning a Logging V2 slice, the user required the smallest coherent reviewable scope, exact Production+test allowlist, explicit unchanged behavior, and read-only stop gates -> future agents should verify reachability and scope before proposing edits.
- when handling PDF/Blob errors, the user explicitly required Blob/PDF contents not to be decoded -> keep Blob bodies opaque; only a strictly validated response-header `X-Request-Id` may be used for reference-only support behavior.

Reusable knowledge:
- `src/hooks/useEmployeeFeedbackPdf.ts` contains the two active producers: POST `/employeeFeedback/:id/pdf/part1to4` and POST `/employeeFeedback/:id/pdf/part1to5`; both currently pass exactly `{ responseType: 'blob' }` and define separate success metadata, filenames, downloads, URL cleanup, and cache invalidations.
- `apiClient` globally shows a backend error toast for 500/502/503 unless request config has `skipGlobalErrorToast`; Production `MutationCache` also shows an error toast when mutation metadata has `errorAction`. Therefore these two PDF mutations currently create two visible error toasts for 500/502/503.
- Recommended minimal fix is adding `skipGlobalErrorToast: true` only to the two active PDF POST configs, leaving MutationCache as the sole error-toast owner. Do not change endpoint, body, response type, retry, auth replay, download, success, or invalidation behavior.
- Both active producers are reachable only for `teamLeader`/`teamleader` through `/vacation-planning` → Feedback tab → `ScheduledFeedbacksList`. The confidential dialog’s GF/HR comment is not an active production entry point.
- Part 1–4 is called with `mutateAsync` from `feedbackManagementDialog.tsx`; Part 1–5 is called with `mutate` from `feedbackPart5Dialog.tsx`. The possible unhandled rejection and success-before-download ordering were identified but must remain separate slices because changing them would alter protected product control flow.
- Existing `useEmployeeFeedbackPdf.errorOwnership.test.tsx` fully mocks `apiClient`, so it cannot demonstrate that the real Axios interceptor is suppressed. Realistic tests must load the actual `apiClient`, Production `queryClient`/MutationCache, and support helper; mock only deep transport, final Sonner/toast sink, and browser download primitives.

Failures and how to do differently:
- A fully mocked `apiClient` makes one-toast assertions tautological and misses the real Axios-interceptor + MutationCache duplicate path. Use the real interceptor harness for future ownership tests.
- Do not bundle legacy `/employeeFeedback/:id/pdf`, preview GETs, unrelated Blob downloads, caller UI, role changes, query-key changes, or support-helper changes into this producer slice; no active caller or separate contract justified them.
- Do not parse Blob JSON or move success/download ordering under the error-toast fix; those are distinct behavior/security boundaries.

- the user required a real Axios interceptor plus Production MutationCache test rather than a complete `apiClient` mock -> test the actual instances and adapters; mock only deep transport/auth and final sinks.
- the user required “Blob niemals dekodieren” and no PDF/feedback/PII/URL/internal-ID leaks -> never call Blob `text`, `arrayBuffer`, `FileReader`, or decode JSON; only validated header request IDs may be reference-copyable.
- after the first review found the DELETE failure test missing, the user required only that test regression restored inside the same allowlist -> preserve adjacent existing failure coverage when mechanically rewriting tests.

Reusable knowledge:
- `src/hooks/useEmployeeFeedbackPdf.ts` now adds `{ ...locallyHandledErrorConfig, responseType: 'blob' }` only to the active Part 1-4 and confidential Part 1-5 POSTs. The existing `{}` body, URL, three-argument Axios call, metadata, success/download/cleanup/invalidation behavior, and legacy PDF POST remain unchanged.
- `skipGlobalErrorToast` is request-local. Production `MutationCache` remains the single visible owner, with retry 0 and original error identity preserved.
- The test harness uses real `apiClient`/`loginClient` Axios instances, real interceptors, real Production `queryClient`/MutationCache, and real support/toast helpers. Adapters, final Sonner/clipboard sinks, and browser download primitives are mocked.

Failures and how to do differently:

- The task input conflicted on `undefined` versus unchanged body. Baseline production used `{}` and the stronger “body unchanged” constraint was followed; changing to `undefined` would be a separate transport-contract change.
- Separate adjacent P2s (success-before-download and event-promise behavior) were explicitly left untouched; do not broaden this slice to fix them.

Preference signals:
- Der Nutzer verlangte einen „FRISCHEN repositorygebundenen READ-ONLY Abschluss-Scout“ mit fail-closed Start-Gate, findings-first, absoluten Datei:Zeile-Links und ohne künstliche Rest-Slices. Bei ähnlichen Reviews zuerst Branch/HEAD/Status/Upstream prüfen, dann nur aktuelle aktive Pfade bewerten.
- Der Nutzer verlangte eine vollständige kompakte Liste „ALLER Restbereiche“. Findings nicht verwässern oder ungenutzte Definitionen als aktive Befunde melden.

Reusable knowledge:
- Verifiziertes Start-Gate: Branch `chore/logging-improvements`, HEAD `6fe9ad9e436e640c4baee0f3756b680b637d8205`, Arbeitsbaum leer, Upstream `0\t0`.
- Scanabdeckung: 1.801 `src`-Dateien, 211 Dateien mit API-Producer-Aufrufen, 266 Dateien mit sichtbaren Fehler-Sinks, 474 Testdateien.
- Zentrale Supportkopie in `src/libs/utils/backendError.ts:313-409` fail-closed auf echtes Axios-Objekt, verschachteltes `data.error`, sichere `message`/`code`/Request-ID und optional validiertes `Date`; `showBackendErrorToast` ist persistent und bietet Kopieraktion (`src/libs/utils/toast.ts:103-127`).
- Sichtbarer Fehlertext ist davon getrennt: `extractBackendErrorDetails` fällt auf Legacy-Top-Level-/Rohmeldungen zurück (`backendError.ts:751-825`), und `extractErrorMessage` zeigt solche Texte (`errorHandling.ts:58-98`). Das widerspricht dem F1-Fail-closed-Ziel, obwohl die Supportkopie selbst verworfen wird.
- Globaler Axios-Interceptor toastet 500/502/503, wenn `skipGlobalErrorToast` fehlt (`apiClient.ts:169-190`). MutationCache toastet Mutationen mit `meta.errorAction`, außer `skipGlobalErrorToast` (`queryClient.ts:50-63`). Jeder aktive Caller braucht deshalb genau einen sichtbaren Owner.
- Blob/PDF-Requests (`responseType: 'blob'`) können den JSON-Envelope nicht sicher wie normale Axios-JSON-Fehler projizieren. Ohne stabilen Backend-Content-Type-/Fehlerbody-Vertrag keine Client-Heuristik einführen.
- Direkte `fetch`-Pfade betreffen nur Feiertagsdienste; `useUpdateRisk`/`useDeleteRisk` sind ungenutzte Hook-Definitionen und kein aktiver Restbereich.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Der Scan führte absichtlich keine Tests oder Edits aus. Outcome basiert auf aktuellem Code, vorhandenen Tests und Pfadverfolgung, nicht auf Laufzeitverifikation.
- Portal-F1 ist nicht scan-clean: drei P1- und vier P2-Befunde.
- P1: zentrale sichtbare Projektion nicht vollständig fail-closed; HR-Sensitive-Data-Entsperrung hat MutationCache, lokalen Toast/Inlinefehler und bei 5xx zusätzlich Interceptor; Blob/PDF/Preview haben keine gemeinsame sichere Fehlergrenze.
- P2: aktive Trainingsmutationen kombinieren `showPromiseToast` mit Interceptor; QM-Audit/Quarterly/Management-JSON-Schreibfamilien haben gemischte oder fehlende Owner; Exam-Assignment-Delete und Result-Release fehlen `skipGlobalErrorToast`; Zertifikats- und Vermittlungsabschluss-Pfade kombinieren Interceptor mit lokalen Handlern.
- Empfohlene Reihenfolge: zentrale Projektion zuerst, dann HR; Trainings/QM/Exams/Zertifikate können danach unabhängig parallel laufen (QM in drei getrennten Slices). Blob/PDF separat nach Backend-Vertragsklärung; keine LMS-Abhängigkeit für diese Portalpfade.

- User required “Keine Edits ... Keine Tests. Findings-first.” -> keep future scouts strictly read-only and lead with concrete findings.
- User required exact production allowlists, active callchains, smallest coherent slices, mechanical tests/docs, and stop-gates; exclude speculative, legacy, and test-only paths -> preserve this report structure.
- User required start/end branch/HEAD/upstream/clean gates and stop on drift -> verify those gates before and after every repository-bound scout.

Reusable knowledge:
- Baseline and final state were unchanged: branch `chore/logging-improvements`, HEAD `7bf7aa8bde6cd6d55a3c5922fd46dc7850a8eb30`, upstream `0/0`, clean status.
- Existing hardened paths are in `lib/errors/server/backend-error-projection.ts`, Sidebar BFF/parser, Exam BFF, and GitHub Classroom BFF. They already validate safe envelopes, reject technical locations, fail closed on malformed/conflicting request IDs, and use static fallbacks; do not re-report them.
- P1 Topic/SLP finding: `app/api/modules/get-entry/route.ts` and `app/api/modules/get-self-learning-entry/route.ts` use permissive `parseBackendErrorResponse`, forwarding backend `message`, `code`, and `requestId`; `lib/data/db.ts` renders `LMS_CONTENT_LOCKED` messages. Apply the existing safe projector or a narrow validated locked contract. Preserve only confirmed locked behavior; do not broaden all 403s.
- P1 auth finding: `lib/auth/reauth.ts` returns `null` for every non-2xx/network error and logs to console. `app/api/auth/authenticate-user/route.ts` treats that as refreshable invalid auth, potentially converting 5xx/network failures to 401 and losing status/request ID. Future fix must distinguish 401 from system failure, avoid console logging, and preserve refresh cookies/order.
- P1 exam banner finding: `components/layout/exams/banner/student-global-exam-banner.tsx` converts all failed fetches to empty arrays and overwrites successful state during polling, so active banners disappear during transient failures. Preserve last-success state and assign one deduplicated owner for final 5xx/network errors; keep polling/socket/sorting/24-hour visibility unchanged.
- P2 toast ownership finding: repeated 30-second Exam dashboard refreshes and Sidebar focus refreshes can call `showBackendErrorToast`; `lib/errors/backend-error-toast.ts` has no stable Sonner ID, so identical persistent errors stack. Deduplicate same failures and update one owner for changed references without changing refresh cadence or 401/403 silence.
- P2 console finding: `components/layout/modules/modules-components/custom-example-components/formbeispiel.tsx` logs complete `FormData` including user input; the shortcode is production allowlisted. `app/modules/[module]/[submodule]/[slug]/error.tsx` logs full Error objects. Remove raw console output while preserving UI behavior.
- P2 logout finding: `app/api/auth/logout-user/route.ts` uses permissive body-first parsing and reflects selected request IDs; `components/ui/user-logout.tsx` displays them. Malformed/conflicting IDs may remain copyable. Harden with the safe projector while preserving CSRF/Origin, Set-Cookie, status, and redirect timer contracts.
- No active production upload/PDF/blob/download BFF paths were found; image transformation was out of scope.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not call the repository scan clean or PR-ready: final report explicitly says `nicht scan-clean und noch nicht PR-reif als finale F1-Vollendung`.
- Tests were intentionally not run. No repository-documented baseline test failures were found, but this is unverified.

Reusable knowledge:
- Verifizierter Zustand: Branch `chore/logging-improvements`; lokaler HEAD und `origin/chore/logging-improvements` exakt `3c9ef9afc76ec2933d5158320268d08039e6af56`; `origin/dev` exakt `f2cf9853453667dbee6e3980b7b4cf7e4c83cb35`; Merge-Base `86b5002d86cb1aa50acb3155ef42b58795cc0630`; lokaler Branch 0 ahead/0 behind; Arbeitsbaum/Index sauber.
- Der erlaubte Fetch musste wegen Sandbox-Rechten mit Approval ausgeführt werden. Erfolgreicher Befehl: `git fetch --no-tags origin dev chore/logging-improvements`. Ohne erfolgreichen Fetch wären vorhandene Remote-SHAs als möglicherweise stale zu melden gewesen.
- Seit Merge-Base divergieren die Seiten stark: Logging 133 Commits/416 Dateien (+67.582/-2.215), dev 67 Commits/230 Dateien (+15.055/-859). `git log --left-right --cherry-pick` zeigte keine herausgefilterten Patch-Äquivalente.
- `git merge-tree` prognostizierte 25 echte Textkonflikte und 21 zusätzliche semantische Overlaps. Ein normaler Merge ist strategisch richtig; Cherry-Picking würde die zusammenhängenden dev-Produktpakete künstlich zerlegen.
- Besonders zu schützen sind die finalen Logging-Pfade/Commits: `df1723cf` Incident-Reads, `c90c08e0` Console-Datenschutz, `ed5c9b4a` studentische Reads, `c8ad6850` DropCases, `801c2f0e` CM/HR-Owner, `8df6f746` opake Dokumentdownloads, `f0131407` QM-PDF-Owner und `3c9ef9af` fail-closed Corrective.

Bei Integration muss jeweils genau ein Owner verbleiben, request-lokales `skipGlobalErrorToast` verwendet werden, wenn ein lokaler Owner zuständig ist, und die sichere/strikte Projektion inklusive Request-ID erhalten bleiben.
- Belegte False-Empty/False-Loading-Risiken: `src/components/jobCoachTimesheets/JobCoachTimesheetView.tsx`, `JobCoachReviewPage.tsx`, `src/components/freelancerBilling/FreelancerBillingWorkspace.tsx`, `CreditNoteBasisSection.tsx`, `SettlementSection.tsx` und `src/routes/__app/my-documents.tsx`. Query-Fehler müssen getrennt von echten leeren Ergebnissen dargestellt werden; Retry und validierte Request-ID sollen sichtbar bleiben.
- `src/components/dashboard/qualityManager/managementReview/draftHelpers.ts` liest direkte Error-Payload-Felder (`missingKpiEvaluations`, `missingKpiComments`, `invalidKpiEvaluations`, `data.message`). Das ist kein Portal-only Logging-Fix: sichere serverseitige Projektion oder ein explizites Produkt-Go ist erforderlich, bevor der QM-Slice umgesetzt wird.
- Geschützte QM-Reihenfolge ist Draft speichern → Submit bzw. Draft speichern → PDF exportieren → Vorschau aktualisieren. Konfliktauflösung darf diese Reihenfolge, Owner oder Produktabläufe nicht verändern.
- Empfohlene Slice-Reihenfolge: normaler Merge mit kombinierender Konfliktauflösung; Contracts/Freelancer-Billing; HR-Rechnungsannahme; Jobcoach-Timesheets; QM-KPI/Managementreview; finale reine Prüf-Slice. Jede Folge-Slice startet erst mit dem exakten SHA der abgenommenen vorherigen Slice.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Der erste Fetch scheiterte an `error: cannot open '.git/FETCH_HEAD': Operation not permitted`; nach explizitem Approval und escalated permissions gelang derselbe erlaubte Befehl. Bei ähnlichen Umgebungen nicht raten oder abbrechen, sondern nur die autorisierte Permission-Eskalation für den einmaligen Fetch anfordern.
- Ein ungefiltertes `merge-tree`-Parsing mit `awk` traf Binär-/Mehrbyte-Ausgabe und meldete eine Multibyte-Konvertierungswarnung. Die anschließende `LC_ALL=C`-Variante lieferte die 25 Konfliktpfade zuverlässig. Bei Git-Ausgaben mit Binärdaten `LC_ALL=C` verwenden.
- Nicht pauschal „ours“ oder „theirs“ übernehmen: dadurch würden entweder Logging-Owner/Privacy-Schutz oder Martins Produktfelder, Direktimporte und neue Workflows verloren gehen.
- Keine Tests ausführen und keine Änderungen vornehmen, wenn der Auftrag ausdrücklich nur Planung erlaubt.

### Task 1: Map real endpoint producers and persistence contracts

task: logging-v2-backend-dev-endpoint-mapping
task_group: Novari Backend Logging V2 read-only review
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user explicitly required “READ-ONLY”, a fresh independent context, exact baseline verification, and no edits/tests/processes/Git mutations -> future agents should verify the checkout first, investigate only, and stop rather than implement.
- The user required a complete matrix with endpoint, method, role/auth, prerequisites, natural failure, safe response, persistence yes/no/category, and Security Event searchability -> future agents should preserve this structure and explicitly separate transient `request.error` logs from persisted audit/security events.
- The user required minimal allowlists and hard stop-gates for later Dev-only fault injection -> default to no backend production change and require dual Dev gating plus fixed scenarios if full failure coverage is later approved.

Reusable knowledge:
- Exact verified baseline: detached `HEAD` `5b95632051b649a742ad3309ff9b01a080bc90e5` exactly matched local/remote `chore/logging-improvements`; working tree clean. No tests were run because they were prohibited.
- The only schema-V2 persisted support error is `GET /auth/lms/github-curriculum/program-types/:programTypeId/repository/inventory` for `pdl`/`lmsSupport` when the exact `503 GITHUB_SYNC_CONNECTION_FAILED` contract occurs. Persistence is best effort, once per request, fixed-field only, with requestId and optional HMAC actor hash; persistence failure preserves the original response and does not retry.
- `/auth/security-events` is available to `lmsSupport`, `LmsSupport`, and `admin`. Exact support filters are `category=error`, `severity=error`, `application=Backend`, `code=GITHUB_SYNC_CONNECTION_FAILED`; `requestId` forces exact ungrouped rows; `view=groups` is list-only, bounded to repeated V2 events and a maximum 30-day UTC window. Routine list/filter/refresh calls do not create success audit events.
- Shared HTTP contract is `{error:{code,message,requestId}}`; `X-Request-Id` and `Date` are exposed through CORS. Invalid error codes normalize to `REQUEST_FAILED` (4xx) or `INTERNAL_ERROR` (5xx).
- WorkRevision Patch target-not-found, Patch conflict, and Review-readiness details are bounded and server-authoritative but intentionally not persisted as Security Events.
- Generic module/profile/calendar/document/PDF/Socket/Jobcoach/Freelancer failures are centrally handled but not persisted. Successful sensitive reads/downloads/writes retain existing audit behavior.
- Freelancer PDF endpoint `/auth/freelancer-timesheets/:id/pdf` is an approved HiDrive read through `streamPdfFromHiDrive`, not a directly generated PDF stream. Generated-stream behavior applies to Hardware and Risk overview PDF paths.

Failures and how to do differently:
- P2 finding: current logging/error docs incorrectly classify Freelancer PDF with directly generated PDF streams. Future test design must treat it as a HiDrive storage-read failure; documentation correction requires a separate authorized task.
- An invalid GitHub branch tests `GITHUB_CURRICULUM_BRANCH_NOT_FOUND`, not the exact persisted V2 support error. The support error requires a readable Dev integration followed by the exact transport/response failure.
- Do not equate stdout `request.error` with MongoDB Security Event persistence; the persistence allowlist is deliberately exact.
- The Gateway’s static internal `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` cannot be exposed unchanged through Portal/LMS because the backend wrapper intentionally translates it to its own safe upstream contract.

### Task 1: Normative V-B adjudication

task: Determine whether V-B is complete using the authoritative Spec and existing evidence only.
task_group: Novari Logging V2 / Portal continuity
 task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user required strictly read-only work: no tests, browser/development runs, data/session/claim actions, edits, Git mutations, delegation, or corrective slice. Similar reviews should freeze the candidate and evaluate existing evidence only.
- The user required exact separation of authoritative Spec wording from Handoff/Plan traceability. Do not infer extra manual/browser obligations from plan fields absent from the Spec.

Reusable knowledge:
- Authoritative Spec: `/Users/mrbubbles/.codex/.chatgpt-projects/g-p-6a4586156fbc8191b6804e181eaa7edc/Novari_Logging_Error_Handling_und_Audit_Spec_V2.md`, 1,211 lines, SHA-256 `6f1cb92db2994da087aee2ab1d799dd78d90b6501f18777894eb056a30214fe6`.
- Spec §10 lines 578–593 requires lifecycle gating, cancellation on hidden/unmount/identity or role change, stale-generation rejection, bounded retries, and no persisted event for successful polling. It does not require a manually manufactured late response, per-dimension browser runs, multi-account testing, or a separate claim/tab extreme case.
- Spec §17.1/§17.3 requires a Development test surface and manual scenarios for applicable real-system evidence, but the Handoff/Plan’s detailed browser protocol is a chosen evidence method, not an additional normative contract.
- Portal candidate `chore/logging-improvements@8ab63d7e5affa0eda3913d7bb9707b0712a2a495` and Backend `@af21c988c51b88fd47a4f2989614654c3b46a846` were clean, upstream-identical, and 0/0. No changes were made.
- Portal tests in `src/hooks/lms/__tests__/useCurriculumWorkRevisionContinuityContext.test.tsx` cover complete identity (`118–141`), claim/visibility (`143–169`), 15-second cadence (`171–200`), abort on hidden/claim loss/unmount (`202–254`), return fetch (`256–281`), identity isolation for user/role/CurriculumVersion/WorkRevision/EditSession/tab (`481–525`), stale result rejection (`527–555`), terminal errors (`590–617`), and bounded transient backoff (`619–666`). The focused suite was already documented as `36/36` green and was not rerun.
- Backend test `curriculumWorkRevisionController.test.js:871–898` verifies the unchanged continuity response without a successful read audit for `pdl` and `lmsSupport`.
- Existing real evidence showed 21 successful poll Request-IDs with zero matching audit events, unchanged CurriculumVersion/WorkRevision fields, and unchanged audit total. `V-B-RET-1` only changed Portal Query/Focus options, not service/API/persistence/audit owners, so this evidence remains valid.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Earlier evidence incorrectly stopped K7 because a canceled request had no backend `X-Request-Id`. The Spec does not require a response-header ID for a request canceled before headers; native cancellation and the subsequent poll stop are sufficient.
- Earlier High-Review treated K8’s missing manually-arriving late response as a normative failure. The correct adjudication is combined evidence: real cancellation proves the safe regular path, while the automated race test proves an old response arriving after identity change is not adopted.

References:
- Spec §10: lines 576–593; §7.1: lines 459–468; §17.1–17.3: lines 997–1071; §19: lines 1143–1199.
- `src/hooks/lms/useCurriculumWorkRevisions.ts:101-203`.
- `src/hooks/lms/__tests__/useCurriculumWorkRevisionContinuityContext.test.tsx:118-688`.
- `audit-work/slice-evidence/v-b.md:65-74` — 21-poll no-write evidence.
- Final adjudication: K1–K7 PASS; K8 accepted via combined evidence; K9 and K10 do not require additional manual execution. V-B can be closed via one short Coordinator decision; D-CA remains gated only until that adjudication is recorded.

task: Route unexpected Self-Absence, HR employee, student, and ClassManager document-download failures to the global error owner while preserving direct product responses and success behavior.
task_group: document download error boundary
 task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user required an exact nine-file allowlist, no subagents, no commit/push before independent High-Review, and explicit freeze identity -> future agents should freeze state before edits and avoid scope expansion.
- The user required unchanged 400/403/404 responses, bytes, MIME/headers, storage, auth/roles, and success audits -> future fixes should include preservation tests for adjacent contracts.

Reusable knowledge:
- Self-Absence and HR employee controllers retain only the structural `HIDRIVE_FILE_NOT_FOUND` 404 locally; other failures are rethrown through `catchAsync`.
- Student and ClassManager controller errors are forwarded with `next(error)` even after headers, preventing swallowed stream failures and JSON double responses.
- Buffered `res.end` paths await completion, listen for response/socket errors and close events, reject premature close when `writableFinished` is false, precheck destroyed/closed state, and remove all listeners in `finally`.
- Student-own streaming remains `await pipeline(Readable.from(fileBuffer), res)` unchanged.
- Global error handling produces the generic request-ID `INTERNAL_ERROR` envelope before headers; after headers, Express receives the original error without a second JSON response.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Running focused tests directly in the detached worktree initially failed because `node_modules` was absent and `mock.module` needed Node's experimental module-mocking flag. Use the repository command shape: `node --experimental-test-module-mocks --import ./tests/setupEncryptionKeys.js --test ...`, with dependencies supplied from the main checkout in a temporary copy.
- A simpler `res.end` callback-only Promise was insufficient because Node 24 can signal socket failures via `error` or close without invoking the callback. Cover callback, response/socket `error`, premature `close`, synchronous throw, and cleanup.

- The six schema-v2 contracts use fixed action/component/area tuples, `event=request.error`, `reasonCode=INTERNAL_ERROR`, `failedStage=unexpected`, `causeClass=unknown`, `failureMode=unexpected_error`, `retryability=unknown`, `supportDisposition=engineering_investigation`, `impact=unknown`, `method=GET`, and `httpStatus=500`.
- Document-read events contain no `targetType` or `targetHash`; only the existing optional HMAC `actorHash` may be added. Course Archive remains the only checked V2 contract requiring target hashing.
- Real router inspection confirmed the three `Symbol.for` owner markers are set by the HR pending-document, student-document, and ClassManager student routers; Self-Absence, employee self-service, and HR employee routes reuse existing private markers.
- Static verification passed: `git diff --check` and `node --check` for all five changed JS files. The review concluded `HIGH-REVIEW PASS` with no P0–P3 findings.

Reusable knowledge:
- D-Producer-Checkpoint ist PASS und unter dem initial freigegebenen Backendvertrag fachlich abgeschlossen, aber alle 85 D-Producer-Matrixzeilen bleiben wegen eigenständiger Triage-, Development-, Integrated- und Gesamtabnahmepflichten `partial`; Gesamtfeature, PRs, Integration und Deployment bleiben NOT READY.
- Die aktuelle Matrix hat 1.288 Requirements in 33 Slice-Labels (`0 fulfilled`, `726 partial`, `460 missing`, `4 intentionally-not-applicable`, `98 explicit non-goal`). Diese Labelanzahl ist kein sinnvoller Arbeitsphasen-Zähler.
- Empfohlene fachliche Blöcke: (1) C-Projection + F1-Portal + F2-LMS als Fehlerprojektion/Supportkopie, etwa 3 technische Tasks; (2) E2-Backend + E1/E3-Portal als Supportsuche/Triageansicht, etwa 2 Tasks; (3) G-Archive, G-Export, G-Retention und H-Alerts als gemeinsamer Operationsblock, aber 4 getrennte Tasks wegen echter Vertrags-/Owner-/Stop-Gate-Grenzen.
- D-Triage umfasst 68 Requirements (47 S4.2, 3 S4.3, 18 S4.4) und ist in der bestehenden Zwei-Dateien-Fassung überbündelt. Zuerst vorhandene sichere Felder, Enums, Fingerprint, Gruppierung, Impact, Portalprojektion, Rollenprüfung und Development-Reproduzierbarkeit gegen Spec §§4.2, 6.2, 8 und 11 abgleichen. Erst eine konkret nachgewiesene Backend-Corelücke rechtfertigt einen engen Corrective.

- I1/I2/I3 sind repositorygebundene Tasks innerhalb einer integrierten Evidencephase, keine drei fachlichen Nutzerphasen. Danach drei Cleanups, ein Matrixabgleich und drei parallele Governance-Doku-Tasks.
- Die FINAL-Communication-, Handoff-Diff-, Protected-Boundaries-, Acceptance- und Negative-Gates können in einer gebündelten read-only Closure-Phase zusammengefasst werden; FINAL-Negative bleibt unmittelbar vor dem unabhängigen FINAL-Review.
- Realistische Größenordnung: etwa 3 dauerhafte Implementierungsblöcke mit ungefähr 9 Runtime-Tasks, plus I1–I3, drei Cleanups und drei Governance-Tasks; grob etwa 18 dateiverändernde Tasks, aber deutlich weniger fachliche Phasen.

- D-Triage nicht aufgrund fehlender B-/T-Zuordnung als fehlende Runtime interpretieren. B34/T28, B35/T29, B36/T30 und B37/T31 belegen nicht automatisch vollständige Triage, beweisen aber auch keine fehlende Runtime.
- Shared Owner wie `libs/observability/auditStore.js` nicht in konkurrierenden E2-/G-/H-Tasks bearbeiten; diese Backend-Lane überwiegend sequenziell planen.
- Vor jedem späteren Go Branch, HEAD, Upstream, direkten Remote-Ref, Clean/Dirty, Baseline, aktuelle Implementierung und exakte Allowlists neu verifizieren.

Owner-Counts ohne Doppelzählung: 38 Backend Core/Eventproduktion, 5 Backend Suche/Gruppierung/Controller, 13 Portal Anzeige/Supportquelle, 3 Development/Integrated Evidence, 9 Governance/finaler Nachweis.

- Der nächste zulässige Slice nach E3 ist **C-Projection (Backend)**, nicht I2, F1, G-Archive oder G-Export.
- Dependency-Begründung: D-Producer und D-Triage liegen vor C; F1 hängt von C; I2 hängt von C, F1, E1 und E3; G-Export hängt von G-Archive. G-Archive ist ein separater parallel möglicher Backendstrang, aber nicht der E3-Nachfolger.
- Backend-Freeze: `/Users/mrbubbles/dev/novari/novari-education-backend`, Branch `chore/logging-improvements`, HEAD/Upstream `35e3c4dd7d40e0888efe91d0328ec4af501382e5`, ahead/behind `0/0`, Arbeitsbaum einschließlich Untracked sauber.

- C-Projection ist Runtime-Arbeit: `error/globalErrorHandler.js` normalisiert den Fehler, schreibt Serverlogging, ruft `persistSupportErrorEvent` auf und übergibt danach das normalisierte Ergebnis an `sendErrorResponse`; `sendErrorResponse` projiziert aktuell nicht den vollständigen geplanten sicheren User-/Supportvertrag. `getSafeRequestPath` aus `libs/observability/httpLogger.js` ist als vorhandener Route-Template-Helper wiederzuverwenden.
- C-Projection soll fail-closed sichere Projektionen liefern und Rohdetails vor der Client-/Logging-Grenze ausschließen: keine Stacks, Exception-Ketten, Roh-URLs, Querywerte, Bodies, Tokens, Cookies, PII, Dateipfade oder Roh-ObjectIds.
- Exakte Allowlist: Production `error/globalErrorHandler.js`; `error/httpError.js`; `libs/observability/httpLogger.js`. Tests `tests/error/globalErrorHandler.test.js`; `tests/error/httpError.test.js`; `tests/observability/httpLogger.test.js`. Docs-Allowlist: keine. Neues Evidence-Artefakt außerhalb des Runtime-Diffs: `audit-work/slice-evidence/c-projection.md`.
- Die 92 C-Requirement-IDs bleiben aktuell `partial`: S5-/S5.1-/S5.2-Projektions- und Offenlegungsfamilien sowie `S13-R4A1`–`S13-R4E`. Eine Slice-Evidence hebt ihre Gesamtstatus nicht automatisch auf `fulfilled`.
- C-Projection ist ohne Produktentscheid vollständig start-ready, jedoch muss vor tatsächlicher Implementierung ein neuer Start-Freeze erfolgen und das Nutzer-Go vorliegen.

- Keine C-Änderung an Controllern, Producer-/Schema-/Router-Dateien, Portal, LMS, Archiv oder Export zulassen. Bei Scope-Ausweitung sofort stoppen und Nutzerentscheidung einholen.

### Task 1: EMAW integration assessment

task: assess additive EMAW integration and effort for Novari
task_group: novari-emaw-research
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user wants EMAW “oben drauf” without rebuilding Novari and expects Novari to remain the leading system -> default to an additive adapter/transport/workflow layer.
- The user clarified that daily attendance, weekly reports, monthly feedback, and similar examples were purely fictional ideas -> never treat illustrative schedules/UI concepts as requirements without BA confirmation.
- The user wants a BA meeting to establish exact data, events, intervals, onboarding, certification, testing, and migration requirements before implementation commitments.

Reusable knowledge:
- Current BA release verified as PRV 26.07.00 / schema 2.18. Technical package is `/Users/mrbubbles/Downloads/emaw/dok_ba035735.zip`; fachlich package is `dok_ba037285.zip`; AGH package is `dok_ba022355.zip`.
- EMAW is an asynchronous HTTPS client-certificate exchange using nested ZIP archives, XML events, required/optional PDFs, and `OK`/`NOK` acknowledgement XMLs; it is not a REST API and is batch/nightly oriented.
- Existing Novari data relevant to mapping exists in `models/courseSchema.js`, `models/utilitys/studentUtilitys.js`, `models/students/studentSchema.js`, `models/students/studentCourseEnrollmentSchema.js`, and `models/utilitys/classUtilitys.js`.
- The additive integration needs measure/routing binding, inbound/outbound event journal, XML/XSD/ZIP adapter, mapping, acknowledgement/error handling, and a limited inbox/preview workflow. This is a design recommendation, not a BA requirement.
- Provider routing is measure-specific and involves measure number/reference, procedure branch, and BA/gE organisational unit. Users should not choose “AA vs Jobcenter” ad hoc for each message.
- Provider changes are future-effective; old event history must be transferred by the old provider because BA will not replay historical events to the new provider. Public forms recommend about two weeks' lead time.
- Electronic event/PDF signatures are removed from PRV 26.07.00, but AGH still requires correctness/completeness confirmation attributes and responsible-person data.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not use broad estimates for a first measure: separate a concrete first-measure integration from a general multi-procedure provider product.
- Do not infer operational permissions or requirements from the XSD alone; distinguish XSD capability, operationally supported events, and measure-specific contract rules.

References:
- BA overview: `https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/institutionen/bildungstraeger/elektronische-massnahmeabwicklung`
- Technical/XSD source: `/Users/mrbubbles/Downloads/emaw/dok_ba035735.zip`
- Relevant Novari files: `models/courseSchema.js`, `models/utilitys/studentUtilitys.js`, `models/students/studentSchema.js`, `models/students/studentCourseEnrollmentSchema.js`, `models/utilitys/classUtilitys.js`

### Task 2: Deep Research report audit

task: audit `/Users/mrbubbles/Downloads/emaw/deep-research-report.md` against BA primary sources
task_group: novari-emaw-research
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user asked for the report to be treated as research material, not instructions -> preserve source-vs-request separation.
- The user values explicit uncertainty and wants unresolved contradictions carried into the BA meeting rather than silently converted into implementation rules.

Reusable knowledge:
- `Anwesenheitsplanung` is not present in current `emaw-v2.18.xsd`; do not implement it as a BA event based only on provider documentation.
- The report's “complete operational message view” is too strong. AGH includes additional events such as `AGHAenderungTeilnehmerdaten`, `AGHAenderungAnsprechpartnerBetreuerteam`, `AGHAenderungAnsprechpartnerTraegerteam`, `AGHVerlaengerungTeilnahme`, `AGHAustrittVorzeitigVonJC`, `AGH-BasisAblehnung-Massnahme`, `AGHAblehnung`, and legacy/new billing events.
- Regular AGH exit handling is a caveat: current AGH process material indicates no provider-sent eM@w message is required for a regular AGH exit.
- AGH report requests are internally inconsistent across BA documents: the technical schema documentation says a request may be omitted when the provider submits proactively, while the AGH process describes a request-driven flow. Do not hard-code an absolute “must receive request first” block before BA clarification.
- Regular-process attendance: daily collection, monthly transmission by the 9th so AA receives it by the 10th, and immediate transmission on exit. Weekly absence data is sent by Sunday for Monday availability and is not required for all products. AsA-flex has an exception allowing monthly attendance omission when governed by the total-hours-contingent process, while retaining the underlying data.
- AGH monthly billing is documented as: first request on the 1st, possible additional request on the 10th, reminder/check on the 15th, possible second additional request on the 18th; provider billing due by the 15th. The second 18th request is optional.
- The provider-change findings do not establish that a manually handled running measure can be newly activated. They apply reliably to a running EMAW measure changing providers; AGH also has an older explicit statement against retroactive activation.
- TypeScript examples in the report do not match the JavaScript-only Novari backend. Use JavaScript modules/runtime validators, versioned original XSDs, fixtures, and tests.
- Replace internal citation handles such as `turn21search9` with stable URLs plus package/document/page/section references in any future technical specification.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Never present provider documentation as equivalent to BA primary documentation.
- Never describe the report as an implementation specification; it is a useful research basis with confirmed claims, secondary claims, and unresolved contradictions.

References:
- Report: `/Users/mrbubbles/Downloads/emaw/deep-research-report.md`
- Regular process PDF inside `dok_ba037285.zip`: `Anlage 1 - Prozessablauf EMAW Trägersicht/260325_PRV_26.07.00_Juli.2026_Anlage_1-Prozessablauf_EMAW_Trägersicht.pdf`
- AGH process PDF inside `dok_ba022355.zip`: `Anlage 2_Fachlicher_Prozessablauf.pdf`
- Current schema: `emaw-v2.18.xsd`
- Key source wording: `AGHAnforderungMassnahmeberichtTyp` documentation states: “Die Anforderung muss nicht erfolgen, wenn der Traeger von sich aus einen Zwischenbericht/Ergebnisbericht uebermittelt.”

### Task 1: Bündelter Gesamtabschlussplan

task: logging-v2-finalization-plan-three-blocks
task_group: Logging V2 traceability planning
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- Der Nutzer sagte ausdrücklich, die „10 Restblöcke“ seien zunächst Ursachen-/Abschlussgruppen und „nicht automatisch 10 separat freizugebende Slices“ -> künftige Pläne sollen wenige fachliche Blöcke bilden und interne Repository-Tasks davon getrennt ausweisen.
- Der Nutzer verlangte „möglichst wenige fachliche Arbeitsblöcke“ und „maximal sinnvoller Parallelisierung“ -> parallelisieren nur bei klar getrennter Eigentümerschaft und ohne Ressourcen-/Dateninterferenz.
- Der Nutzer verlangte, vorhandene kandidatengültige Runtime-, Automated-, Slice- oder Acceptance-Evidenz zuerst zu verwenden; ein `partial`-Status allein soll keinen neuen Browser-/Realpfad-/Integrationstest auslösen.
- Der Nutzer verlangte genau einen vollständigen Spec→Matrix→Traceability→Runtime-Gesamtreview ganz am Ende; Zwischenreviews nur bei materiellem Finding, Vertragsänderung oder Stop-Gate.

Reusable knowledge:
- Zehn Restgruppen wurden zu drei fachlichen Blöcken gebündelt: A = Clientfehler/Request-ID/UI-Projektion + Produzenten/Triage/Suche/Supportansicht + Polling + Portalzugang; B = Archivierung und Retention; C = Systemwarnungen.
- Block A kann intern in A-BE, A-Portal, A-LMS und A-X aufgeteilt werden; die drei Repository-Tasks sind keine neuen fachlichen Slices. Block B bleibt fachlich gemeinsam, aber Archiv und Retention werden sequenziell adjudiziert bzw. ausgeführt. Block C kann intern in C-BE, C-Portal und C-X geteilt werden.
- Nach A/B/C folgen drei Abschlussklammern: Integrated-/Final-Acceptance, gemeinsames Handoff/Governance, finaler Refreeze plus genau ein unabhängiger vollständiger Gesamtreview.
- Acceptance-Closeout A01 ist HIGH-EVIDENCE PASS für D0–D16 ohne P0–P3, aber kein Gesamt-Compliance-, PR- oder Deployment-Verdict. Slice-PASS darf nicht automatisch als Gesamtbereitschaft gelten.
- Autoritative Spec: SHA-256 `d50f9b01a41a021ca05b9edb46bbd747e2b215e02acf7ce9a05f456fa1cfd92e`; Matrix 1.383 Requirements, Persistence-Submatrix 1.145, offene Liste 1.002.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Nicht aus jeder offenen Matrixzeile oder jedem Evidence-Cluster einen neuen fachlichen Micro-Slice machen.
- Archiv und Retention nie parallel auf demselben oder potenziell beeinflussten Datenbestand ausführen; zuerst Archivzustand vollständig verifizieren, dann Retention.
- Neue Browser-/Realdata-/Integrationstests nur bei konkret nachgewiesener, aktueller Vertragslücke; vorhandene A01-/Slice-Evidenz zuerst kandidatenbezogen adjudizieren.
- Bei reinem Evidence-Transfer fokussierten unabhängigen Evidence-Check verwenden; bei Codeänderung fokussierte Tests und normalen unabhängigen Code-/Vertragsreview; vollständigen Gesamtreview nur am final eingefrorenen Kandidaten.
- Sofort stoppen bei Spec-/Hash-/Kandidatenidentitätsabweichung, dirty Worktree, Evidence-Hashdrift, ungeklärtem Spec/Matrix/Owner-Widerspruch, Allowlistüberschreitung, notwendiger Runtime-/Rollen-/Schema-/Routen-/Control-Plane-/Fault-Injection-Änderung oder nicht isolierbarer Realdata-/Notification-/Archivinterferenz.

### Task 1: Phase-3-Produktspezifikation

task: create-and-refine-bubblophy-phase-3-feature-extension-spec
task_group: Bubblophy orchestration product design
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- Der Nutzer sagte ausdrücklich: „Bubblophy ersetzt nicht die normale Chat-Kommunikation“ -> Chats bleiben für Diskussion, Rückfragen, Brainstorming, Planung, Erklärungen und Reviews; Bubblophy hält nur relevante und dauerhafte strukturierte Ergebnisse fest.
- Der Nutzer stellte klar, dass Bubblophy keine passive Inbox ist -> ein echtes Stop-Gate muss zusätzlich aktiv im aktuell verwendeten Chat mitgeteilt werden; der Nutzer soll nicht ständig Bubblophy überwachen.
- Der Nutzer verlangte bei Stop-Gates eine kurze verständliche Chat-Erklärung: was passiert ist, warum eine Entscheidung nötig ist, Optionen, Empfehlung und welcher Teil weiterlaufen kann.
- Der Nutzer korrigierte die read-only-Formulierung -> MCP ist nicht grundsätzlich read-only. Codex, Claude Code und andere geeignete Clients sollen kontrollierte Phase-3-Writes nutzen können; read-only gilt nur als mögliches client-spezifisches frühes ChatGPT-Rollout.

Reusable knowledge:
- Bubblophy soll als gemeinsame Zustandsschicht neben normalen Agent-Chats funktionieren, nicht als Ersatz für Chat und nicht als freier Agent-zu-Agent-Chatbus.
- Echte Blocker werden sowohl als strukturierter Decision Request in Bubblophy gespeichert als auch aktiv im laufenden Chat eskaliert. Ein Finding-, Status- oder Evidence-Eintrag allein ist kein Stoppgrund.
- MCP-Writes müssen jeweils einen eigenen semantisch engen Vertrag, aktuelle Membership-/Rollenprüfung, Attribution, Konfliktschutz und Auditierung besitzen. Ein generisches `update_anything` ist ausgeschlossen.
- Sensible Vorgänge bleiben getrennt beziehungsweise Human-only, solange kein eigener Vertrag beschlossen wurde: normative Decision aktivieren, bestehende Decision superseden, Scope-/Produktgrenzen ändern, Run freigeben, Deployment oder destruktive externe Aktionen.
- Die Spezifikation trennt fachliche Work Blocks von technischen Issues/Tasks und einzelnen Runs. Findings innerhalb eines freigegebenen Blocks erzeugen nicht automatisch ein neues Feature oder Micro-Slice.
- Große Matrices benötigen eine menschliche Aggregationsebene; offene Matrixzeilen dürfen nicht ohne fachliche Verdichtung als Produktdefekte dargestellt werden.
- Bestehende Bubblophy-Bausteine sollen wiederverwendet werden: Projekte/Membership, Issues, versionierte Pläne, Runs, Audit, Rollen, Agent-Tokens und Remote-MCP/OAuth.

Failures and how to do differently:
- `/mnt/data` war auf dem Host nicht beschreibbar (`mkdir: /mnt: Read-only file system`). Die Datei liegt deshalb im persistenten Projektarbeitsbereich statt im gewünschten Exportordner.
- Ein früher Patch scheiterte an nicht passenden Kontextzeilen; danach wurde anhand tatsächlich gefundener Zeilen erfolgreich gepatcht.
- Bei ähnlichen Spezifikationen die Kommunikationsebene explizit separat von der Zustandsebene formulieren, damit „Koordination über strukturierten Zustand“ nicht fälschlich als Chatersatz verstanden wird.

### Task 1: Browser-boundary hardening and verification

task: harden browser-safe local-agent contracts and exact action approval
 task_group: Inlyra security and local-agent runtime
task_outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user’s accepted workflow preserves a Codex-native card loop: one card, explanation, proposed action, Composer, saved decision, next card; avoid drifting into a Gmail dashboard or email-client UI.
- The handoff and rollout consistently require German UI text with umlauts, in-app Browser checks, provider-neutral source terminology, and no provider actions without explicit approval.

Reusable knowledge:
- Browser projections must remove local paths, shell commands, detailed State Doctor diagnostics, provider account/message targets, credential references, and raw runtime errors.
- Action approval uses an opaque server-keyed HMAC `approvalRef` bound to card ID, action ID, action kind, creation time, and stored provider target. Approval verification and the idempotent local write are serialized against one state snapshot; stale, tampered, concurrent, and previous-server references fail closed.
- Gmail-session parsing must not inspect `document.body.innerText` for login detection. Login detection now relies on structural signals plus existing URL/origin validation; unrelated message text must not trigger `loginRequired`.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Independent review initially found digest/read responses leaking `providerMessageId`, `providerThreadId`, and State Doctor issue details. Future browser-boundary changes must review nested DTO projections and guards, not only top-level fields.
- A second review found whole-page text login detection could misclassify unrelated mail wording. Keep login detection structural and add a regression test whenever parser logic changes.

References:
- `packages/local-agent-runtime/src/actions/action-approval-ref.ts`
- `packages/local-agent-runtime/src/local-agent/server/browser-safe-responses.ts`
- `packages/local-agent-runtime/src/review/browser-safe-digest.ts`
- `packages/local-agent-runtime/src/sources/gmail-session/gmail-session-cdp-runtime.ts`
- `tests/gmail-session-cdp-read-runtime.test.ts`

Preference signals:
